title: Addition and Subtraction Word Problems
seo_title: Word Problems – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve word problems on addition and subtraction of numbers up to 999. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on addition and subtraction word problems with numbers up to 999: altogether, how many more, how many left and missing numbers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Altogether: add. Left or difference: subtract.
key_sub: Read, think, then work it out.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the problem carefully and find the key words.
  • Altogether, in all, total and sum mean add. Left, more than, fewer and difference mean subtract.
  • Write a number sentence, work it out, and check that the answer makes sense.

Examples

Example

A school has 345 boys and 287 girls. How many pupils?

345 + 287

Answer: 632 pupils

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when the question asks how many moreHow many more means find the difference.
Forgetting the units in the answerWrite pupils, naira or metres.
Using the wrong numbersUnderline the numbers you need.

faq.a: How much bigger one number is than another.
Yes, see if it makes sense.

items.q: A library had 476 books. It got 185 new books. How many books does it have now?
Amaka scored 347 points in a game. Then she scored 286 more points. How many points does she have now?
There are 268 children in the infants and 345 children in the juniors. How many children are there altogether?
A library has 742 books. 158 books are lent out. How many books are still on the shelves?
Yusuf has 905 points in a game. Joy has 678 points. How many more points does Yusuf have?
A cinema has 450 seats. 287 seats are taken. How many seats are empty?
A farmer had 634 eggs. He sold 279 eggs. How many eggs are left?
A book has 312 pages. Temi has read 145 pages. How many pages does she have left to read?
A sticker book holds 500 stickers. Yusuf has 263 stickers. How many more does he need to fill it?
Uju had some beads. She bought 145 more. Now she has 403 beads. How many beads did she have at the start?
items.e: Use the inverse. Take away the 145 that were added: 403 − 145 = 258. Check: 258 + 145 = 403.

items.q: Mohammed had some points in a game. He lost 175 points. Now he has 389 points. How many points did he have at the start?
items.e: Use the inverse. Add back the 175 that were lost: 389 + 175 = 564. Check: 564 − 175 = 389.

items.q: The library had 625 books. It lent out 248 books. Then 136 books came back. How many books are there now?
items.e: Step 1, after lending: 625 − 248 = 377. Step 2, after the books came back: 377 + 136 = 513.

items.q: Dayo scored 286 points. Zainab scored 157 more points than Dayo. How many points did they score altogether?
items.e: Step 1, Zainab’s points: 286 + 157 = 443. Step 2, both together: 286 + 443 = 729.

items.q: A shop had 512 bags of crisps. It sold 168 bags on Monday and 195 bags on Tuesday. How many bags are left?
items.e: Step 1, bags sold: 168 + 195 = 363. Step 2, bags left: 512 − 363 = 149. Check: 149 + 363 = 512.

items.q: There were 32 balloons at a party. Peter blew up 15 more balloons. How many balloons are there now?
items.e: 15 more were added, so add: 32 + 15 = ☐. 32 + 15 = 47. Answer: 47 balloons.

items.q: There were 51 people at the pool. Then 39 more people came. How many people are at the pool now?
items.e: 39 more were added, so add: 51 + 39 = ☐. 51 + 39 = 90. Regroup: 1 + 9 = 10 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 90 people.

items.q: There were 18 children on a bus. At the next stop, 17 more children got on. How many children are on the bus now?
items.e: 17 more were added, so add: 18 + 17 = ☐. 18 + 17 = 35. Regroup: 8 + 7 = 15 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 35 children.

items.q: Halima had 65 stickers. She got 26 more stickers from a friend. How many stickers does Halima have now?
items.e: 26 more were added, so add: 65 + 26 = ☐. 65 + 26 = 91. Regroup: 5 + 6 = 11 units. Trade 10 units for 1 ten. Answer: 91 stickers.

items.q: Nkechi had 72 shells. At the beach, she found 12 more shells. How many shells does Nkechi have now?
items.e: 12 more were added, so add: 72 + 12 = ☐. 72 + 12 = 84. Answer: 84 shells.

items.q: There were 73 cars in a parking lot. Then 67 cars drove away. How many cars are in the lot now?
items.e: 67 were taken away, so subtract: 73 − 67 = ☐. 73 − 67 = 6. You cannot take 7 from 3 in the units place, so trade 1 ten for 10 units first. Answer: 6 cars.

items.q: Uju scored 458 points in the first round of a game and 172 points in the second round. What was the total score?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Units: 8 + 2 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Answer: 630.

items.q: A stadium has 864 seats. 625 seats are filled. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Take one part away from the whole: subtract. Units: 4 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 14 − 5 = 9. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Hundreds: 8 − 6 = 2. Answer: 239. Check: 239 + 625 = 864.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 400 = 719
items.e: Use subtraction: 719 − 400 = 319. Check: 319 + 400 = 719.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which is the best estimate for 704 − 286?
items.e: 704 rounds to 700 and 286 rounds to 300. 700 − 300 = 400. The exact answer, 418, is close to 400.

items.q: On Saturday, 947 people visited the zoo. On Sunday, 482 people visited. How many more people visited on Saturday than on Sunday?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: subtract. Units: 7 − 2 = 5. Tens: 4 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 hundred becomes 10 tens: 14 − 8 = 6. Hundreds: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 465. Check: 465 + 482 = 947.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which is the best estimate for 623 + 289?
items.e: 623 rounds to 600 and 289 rounds to 300. 600 + 300 = 900. The exact answer, 912, is close to 900.

items.q: A library had 295 books. It got 392 new books. How many books does it have now?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Units: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 9 + 9 = 18, write 8 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6. Answer: 687.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which is the best estimate for 812 − 395?
items.e: 812 rounds to 800 and 395 rounds to 400. 800 − 400 = 400. The exact answer, 417, is close to 400.

items.q: Yusuf's book has 879 pages. He has read 592 pages. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: Take one part away from the whole: subtract. Units: 9 − 2 = 7. Tens: 7 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 hundred becomes 10 tens: 17 − 9 = 8. Hundreds: 7 − 5 = 2. Answer: 287. Check: 287 + 592 = 879.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 303 = 603
items.e: Use subtraction: 603 − 303 = 300. Check: 300 + 303 = 603.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 788 − ☐ = 547
A shop had 483 stickers. It sold 219 stickers in the morning and 153 in the afternoon. How many stickers were sold in all?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Units: 9 + 3 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 1 + 5 + 1 = 7. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. Answer: 372.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 933 − ☐ = 766
What number goes in the box? 629 − ☐ = 360
A farm had 491 eggs. 245 eggs were sold at the market. How many eggs are left?
items.e: Take one part away from the whole: subtract. Units: 1 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. Hundreds: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 246. Check: 246 + 245 = 491.

items.q: Tunde's school has 467 pupils in the morning. 387 more pupils come for an afternoon event. How many pupils are there in all?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Units: 7 + 7 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 8 + 1 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Answer: 854.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which is the best estimate for 487 + 312?
items.e: 487 rounds to 500 and 312 rounds to 300. 500 + 300 = 800. The exact answer, 799, is close to 800.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 340 = 736
items.e: Use subtraction: 736 − 340 = 396. Check: 396 + 340 = 736.

items.q: A library had 199 books. It got 411 new books. How many books does it have now?
items.e: Put the two amounts together: add. Units: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 9 + 1 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 1 + 4 + 1 = 6. Answer: 610.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 163 = 527
items.e: Use subtraction: 527 − 163 = 364. Check: 364 + 163 = 527.

items.q: A library has 346 books. 7 new books arrive. How many books are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 346 + 4 = 350. 7 is 4 + 3, so add 3 more: 350 + 3 = 353.

items.q: Temi walks 485 steps to the park gate. She walks 8 more steps to the swings. How many steps is that?
items.e: Put the steps together, so add. Make the next ten first. 485 + 5 = 490. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 490 + 3 = 493.

items.q: A school has 423 pupils. 30 pupils go on a school trip. How many pupils stay at school?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 423 has 2 tens. You cannot take 3 tens from 2. Exchange 1 hundred for 10 tens: 3 hundreds and 12 tens. 12 tens − 3 tens = 9 tens. 423 − 30 = 393.

items.q: Femi is on page 268 of a book. He reads 50 more pages. Which page is he on now?
items.e: Read on, so add. Tens: 6 tens + 5 tens = 11 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 2 to 3, and 1 ten is left. 268 + 50 = 318.

items.q: A shop has 615 stickers. It sells 200 stickers. How many stickers are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 200 is 2 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 6 − 2 = 4. The other digits stay the same. 615 − 200 = 415.

items.q: A football match has 834 fans. 300 fans leave early. How many fans are still watching?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 300 is 3 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 8 − 3 = 5. The other digits stay the same. 834 − 300 = 534.

items.q: A train has 408 seats. 9 seats are empty. How many seats have people in them?
items.e: Take the empty seats away, so subtract. Go back to the ten first. 408 − 8 = 400. 9 is 8 + 1, so take away 1 more: 400 − 1 = 399.

items.q: A garden centre has 572 plants. It sells 60 plants. How many plants are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 60 is 6 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 7 − 6 = 1. The other digits stay the same. 572 − 60 = 512.

items.q: Chidi has 695 points in a game. He wins 8 more points. How many points does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 695 + 5 = 700. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 700 + 3 = 703.

items.q: A bakery bakes 380 rolls in the morning and 40 rolls in the afternoon. How many rolls is that?
items.e: Put the two amounts together, so add. Tens: 8 tens + 4 tens = 12 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 3 to 4, and 2 tens are left. 380 + 40 = 420.

items.q: There are 517 books on the shelves. Pupils borrow 300 books. How many books are still on the shelves?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 300 is 3 hundreds. Only the hundreds digit changes: 5 − 3 = 2. The other digits stay the same. 517 − 300 = 217.

items.q: Hadiza has 452 stamps. Uju has 30 more stamps than Hadiza. How many stamps does Uju have?
items.e: 30 more than means add 30. 30 is 3 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 5 + 3 = 8. The other digits stay the same. 452 + 30 = 482.

items.q: There are 245 cars in a car park. 9 more cars drive in. How many cars are there now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 245 + 5 = 250. 9 is 5 + 4, so add 4 more: 250 + 4 = 254.

items.q: Sani runs 760 m. Then he runs 50 m more. How far does he run altogether?
items.e: Put the two distances together, so add. Tens: 6 tens + 5 tens = 11 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 7 to 8, and 1 ten is left. 760 + 50 = 810.

items.q: A book has 300 pages. Fatima has read 270 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Count on from 270 to 300: 7 tens + 3 tens = 10 tens. So 30 pages are left. Check: 270 + 30 = 300.

items.q: Yetunde has 548 beads. She gives away 6 beads. Then she buys 30 more. How many beads does she have now?
items.e: Step 1: 548 − 6 = 542. Step 2: 542 + 30 = 572. (578 adds the 6 instead of taking it away.)

items.q: Yusuf walks 485 steps to the park gate. He walks 8 more steps to the swings. How many steps is that?
items.e: Put the steps together, so add. Make the next ten first. 485 + 5 = 490. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 490 + 3 = 493.

items.q: Aminat is on page 268 of a book. She reads 50 more pages. Which page is she on now?
items.e: Read on, so add. Tens: 6 tens + 5 tens = 11 tens. Exchange 10 tens for 1 hundred. The hundreds go up from 2 to 3, and 1 ten is left. 268 + 50 = 318.

items.q: Bayo has 695 points in a game. He wins 8 more points. How many points does he have now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Make the next ten first. 695 + 5 = 700. 8 is 5 + 3, so add 3 more: 700 + 3 = 703.

items.q: Dayo has 452 stamps. Uju has 30 more stamps than Dayo. How many stamps does Uju have?
items.e: 30 more than means add 30. 30 is 3 tens. Only the tens digit changes: 5 + 3 = 8. The other digits stay the same. 452 + 30 = 482.

items.q: Find the missing number: 465 + ? = 495
items.e: Compare the digits. Only the tens digit is different. So the missing number is 30. Check: 465 + 30 = 495.

items.q: Find the missing number: 352 + ? = 359
items.e: Compare the digits. Only the units digit is different. So the missing number is 7. Check: 352 + 7 = 359.

items.q: Find the missing number: 218 + ? = 718
items.e: Compare the digits. Only the hundreds digit is different. So the missing number is 500. Check: 218 + 500 = 718.

items.q: Find the missing number: 386 + ? = 394
Find the missing number: 457 + ? = 517
items.e: Count on in tens from 457: 467, 477, 487, 497, 507, 517. That is 6 tens = 60. Check: 457 + 60 = 517.

items.q: Find the missing number: 684 − ? = 654
items.e: Only the tens digit changes: 8 tens become 5 tens. 3 tens = 30. Check: 684 − 30 = 654.

items.q: Find the missing number: 523 − ? = 517
Find the missing number: ? + 40 = 372
items.e: Use the inverse. 372 − 40 = 332. Check: 332 + 40 = 372. (412 comes from adding 40 instead.)

items.q: Find the missing number: ? − 6 = 427
Find the missing number: ? − 200 = 315
Find the missing number: ? + 300 = 864
items.e: Use the inverse. 864 − 300 = 564. Only the hundreds digit changes: 8 − 3 = 5.

items.q: 8 + 5 = 13. Use this fact. What is 348 + 5?
items.e: 8 units + 5 units = 13 units = 1 ten and 3 units. So the tens go up by 1: 348 + 5 = 353.

items.q: 7 + 4 = 11. Use this fact. What is 470 + 40?
items.e: 7 tens + 4 tens = 11 tens = 1 hundred and 1 ten. So the hundreds go up by 1: 470 + 40 = 510.

items.q: 13 − 6 = 7. Use this fact. What is 413 − 6?
items.e: 413 is 4 hundreds and 13 units. 13 units − 6 units = 7 units. So 413 − 6 = 407.

items.q: 347 + 6 = 353. Which calculation is also true?
items.e: Subtraction is the inverse of addition. Start at 353 and take away the 6 you added: 353 − 6 = 347.

items.q: 482 + 50 = 532. Which calculation is also true?
items.e: Use the inverse. Start at 532 and take away 50: 532 − 50 = 482.

items.q: Add 10, then take away 1. What is 456 + 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. 456 + 10 = 466. Then 466 − 1 = 465. (466 forgets to take away 1.)

items.q: Take away 10, then add 1. What is 532 − 9?
items.e: 9 is 1 less than 10. 532 − 10 = 522. You took away 1 too many, so add it back: 522 + 1 = 523.

items.q: How many more make 500? 470 + ? = 500
items.e: 7 tens + 3 tens = 10 tens = 1 hundred. So 470 + 30 = 500. (70 + 30 = 100, a number bond.)

items.q: How many more make 700? 640 + ? = 700
items.e: 4 tens + 6 tens = 10 tens = 1 hundred. So 640 + 60 = 700. (40 + 60 = 100, a number bond.)
